subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which part of a flower produces pollen grains?
questions.explain: The anther is the part of the stamen (the male reproductive part) that produces and releases pollen.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human sperm cell?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid and carry 23 chromosomes, half the 46 found in a normal body cell.

questions.q: Which feature is typical of a wind-pollinated flower?
options: Feathery stigmas that hang outside the flower
questions.explain: Wind-pollinated flowers have large feathery stigmas exposed to the air to catch pollen carried on the wind.

questions.q: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are described as:
options: Formed by the fusion of two gametes
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and no gametes, so offspring are clones that are genetically identical to the parent.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?
options: It increases genetic variation in the offspring
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction mixes alleles from two parents, producing variation that can help a species adapt to change.

questions.q: In humans, the male gamete is the:
questions.explain: The male gamete in humans is the sperm cell, while the female gamete is the egg cell (ovum).

questions.q: Which hormone brings about the release of an egg (ovulation) during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: A surge of LH stimulates ovulation, the release of a mature egg from the ovary.

questions.q: What is the role of FSH in the menstrual cycle?
options: It stimulates an egg to mature in the ovary
It causes the uterus lining to break down
questions.explain: FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) causes an egg to mature in the ovary and stimulates the ovaries to produce oestrogen.

questions.q: What is the main function of the placenta during pregnancy?
options: To allow exchange of substances between the mother and the fetus
To protect the fetus from mechanical shock
To supply the fetus with amniotic fluid
questions.explain: The placenta allows oxygen and nutrients to pass to the fetus and waste such as carbon dioxide to pass to the mother.

questions.q: In a DNA molecule, which base pairs with adenine?
questions.explain: In DNA, adenine always pairs with thymine, and cytosine always pairs with guanine.

questions.q: What is an allele?
options: A different version of a gene
A whole set of an organism's genes
questions.explain: An allele is one of the alternative forms of a particular gene, for example the allele for brown or blue eyes.

questions.q: Which term describes the observable characteristics of an organism?
questions.explain: The phenotype is the physical, observable expression of the genes, whereas the genotype is the combination of alleles present.

questions.q: An organism with the genotype Bb is described as:
questions.explain: Heterozygous means the two alleles for a gene are different (here one dominant B and one recessive b).

questions.q: Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?
questions.explain: A Tt x Tt cross gives genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, producing a 3:1 ratio of tall to short.

questions.q: A homozygous dominant plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant (tt). What are the genotypes of all the offspring?
questions.explain: Each offspring receives one T allele and one t allele, so all offspring are heterozygous Tt.

questions.q: A couple have a baby boy. Which sex chromosome must the boy have inherited from his father?
questions.explain: Males are XY; the mother always provides an X, so a boy must have received the Y chromosome from his father.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of continuous variation in humans?
options: Whether earlobes are attached or free
questions.explain: Height shows a range of values across a population, which is continuous variation, unlike distinct categories such as blood group.

questions.q: What is a mutation?
options: A change in the sequence of DNA
A copy of an existing gene
questions.explain: A mutation is a change in the base sequence of DNA and is a source of new genetic variation.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species.

questions.q: A population of bacteria is treated with an antibiotic. A few bacteria carry an allele giving resistance and survive. Why does the resistant population increase over time?
options: Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, passing on the resistance allele
The antibiotic causes each bacterium to become resistant
Bacteria choose to become resistant when threatened
The antibiotic adds resistance genes to all the bacteria
questions.explain: This is natural selection: resistant bacteria survive the antibiotic and reproduce, so the resistance allele becomes more common.
